newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan buys 30,000 tonnes raw sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan buys 30,000 tonnes raw sugar at tender.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp on Wednesday bought a 30,000-tonne Australia raw sugar shipment at a tender in New York City, company officials said.
Queensland Sugar Corp, Australia's eighth largest exporter in 1996, would supply Taiwan Sugar's shipment, officials said.
The shipment was specified for a June 5-20 arrival in Taiwan.
Company officials declined to disclose purchase prices.
The official said the tender was an invitation-only tender in New York city on May 6.

Taiwan Sugar's latest tender required the raw sugar's polarisation to be higher than 97.5 degrees. The standard was reduced from the normal 98.5 degrees in order to include raw sugar from Thailand, which has a 98-degree polarisation, company officials told Reuters.
Queensland's sugar has a polarisation of 98.7 degrees, officials said.
Tokyo traders had said on Wednsday that a Japanese trade house was seeking to send Thai raw sugar to Taiwan at the tender.
Thai raw sugar premiums for May/July delivery were quoted at 0.65/0.70 cents per pound (bid/offer) over New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange on a free on board (FOB) basis.
Australia's sugar state of Queensland produced 5.156 million tonnes of sugar in 1996, making it one of the world's largest sugar exporters along with Brazil, Thailand and the European Union.
